summary: Built a double-NAT path: node3 (lan-a, 10.10.1.3) sends to node4:8080 (lan-b, 10.10.3.4); node1 (VyOS) SNATs to its transit address 10.10.2.1 as traffic enters the transit network; node2 (OPNsense) SNATs again to its lan-b address 10.10.3.254 as traffic enters lan-b, so node4 records the connection source as node2. Verified end-to-end via curl and node4's access log, plus conntrack/pf state showing both NAT hops. Ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all 4 nodes with changed boot markers and full post-restart recovery confirmed for each.
actions_performed: Surveyed all 4 nodes (OS, interfaces, routes) to establish baseline; found all nodes initially only addressed on a shared default management network

Used temporary test addressing plus IPv4/IPv6 neighbor-discovery evidence to determine true physical NIC pairing: node1.eth2<->node3.enp8s0 (lan-a), node1.eth1<->node2.vtnet1 (transit), node2.vtnet2<->node4.enp8s0 (lan-b)
Configured VyOS node1: eth2=10.10.1.254/24, eth1=10.10.2.1/24, static route 10.10.3.0/24 via 10.10.2.2, source-NAT masquerade rule on eth1 for source 10.10.1.0/24, committed and saved

Configured OPNsense node2 via config.xml surgery: added opt1 (vtnet1 transit, 10.10.2.2/24) and opt2 (vtnet2 lan-b, 10.10.3.254/24) interfaces, added a forward pass rule allowing opt1->opt2 tcp/8080, switched outbound NAT to hybrid mode (automatic rule already SNATs all egress-vtnet2 traffic to the interface address), reloaded interfaces and filter

Configured static, reboot-persistent addressing on node3 (10.10.1.3/24 + route to 10.10.3.0/24 via 10.10.1.254) and node4 (10.10.3.4/24) using systemd-networkd drop-in .network files, since systemd-networkd would otherwise reconcile away manual `ip addr` changes
Started an HTTP server on node4:8080 as a systemd unit (node4-http.service) for persistence, initially serving from /tmp/www

Verified end-to-end: curl from node3 to node4:8080 succeeded; node4 access log recorded source 10.10.3.254 (node2's lan-b address); node1 conntrack and node2 pf state both showed the two separate NAT translation hops
Captured healthy-baseline evidence (boot marker + service/config state) on all 4 nodes before restarting

Restarted node4 one at a time via native `reboot`, polled until exec access returned, confirmed changed boot_id, found /tmp/www was wiped by tmpfs-on-reboot causing a 404, fixed by moving served content to persistent /srv/www and restarting the service, then re-verified curl success
Restarted node3, confirmed changed boot_id, confirmed static IP/route persisted via systemd-networkd config, confirmed end-to-end curl still succeeded
Restarted node1 (VyOS), confirmed changed boot_id, confirmed interface addresses/static route/NAT rule/ip_forward persisted via `save`, confirmed end-to-end curl still succeeded

Restarted node2 (OPNsense) last, confirmed changed kern.boottime, confirmed opt1/opt2 addressing, forward pass rule, and outbound NAT rule persisted in config.xml, confirmed final end-to-end curl succeeded with node4 log showing source 10.10.3.254 across multiple post-restart requests

evidence.requirement: Determine real network topology (lan-a/transit/lan-b NIC pairing)
evidence.summary: IPv6/IPv4 neighbor discovery confirms node1.eth2<->node3.enp8s0 and node2.vtnet2<->node4.enp8s0 pairings, plus prior REACHABLE entry for node1.eth1<->node2.vtnet1

evidence.requirement: First NAT hop on node1 (VyOS) as traffic enters transit network
evidence.summary: nftables masquerade rule on eth1 for 10.10.1.0/24 active; conntrack shows node3's 10.10.1.3 translated to node1's transit address 10.10.2.1

evidence.requirement: Second NAT hop on node2 (OPNsense) as traffic enters lan-b
evidence.summary: pf shows nat on vtnet2 to interface address; pf state confirms 10.10.2.1:44480 translated to 10.10.3.254:21839 entering lan-b

evidence.requirement: node4 records connection as arriving from node2, not node3 or node1
evidence.summary: curl from node3 succeeds; node4's HTTP access log records source 10.10.3.254 (node2's lan-b IP) both before and after all node restarts
